data.headline: Raise price 5% now to offset supply squeeze
data.why: Heavy rain in the Central Highlands is delaying the new harvest and cutting fresh cherry supply. Domestic prices are already climbing. A 5% increase captures that market move before rivals react and protects margin on the 80% of cost tied to this region.
data.watch_out: If rain eases and harvest accelerates faster than expected, supply could surge and force a price rollback, leaving you above the rival's 7.9 and risking café orders.
data.recheck_when: Watch the next two weekly harvest reports from the Central Highlands; re-evaluate if cherry arrivals jump sharply.
data.cost_line: Beans +15% × 80% of your cost is beans = your cost +12% (+$0.59 a bag)

what_happened.text: London robusta futures hit $4,546 a tonne, the peak of the spring run-up; the International Coffee Organization called April's level a 45-year high.
Robusta reached its highest price since 1979 as a drought cut Vietnam's 2023/24 harvest.
Reuters-credited reporting: robusta futures had hit records earlier in the year, mostly after an underwhelming Vietnam harvest and fears over the next one after the drought.
The ICO reported robusta at a 47-year high for two months in a row, averaging 214.7 US cents a pound in July.

caveats: Prices are the example roaster's (the coffee_hcmc example) scaled to early-2024 bean prices. A kilo of roasted coffee needs about 1.19 kg of green beans (a 16% roasting loss), so at 3.33 $/kg that is $3.96 of beans; $0.97 is packaging and other cost. Beans are then 80% of the unit cost, and the price keeps the example's markup. These are a made-up owner's numbers, not a real roaster's.

The price series is the world robusta price (Pink Sheet, monthly, $/kg). A Vietnamese roaster pays farm-gate prices in dong, which follow it with a lag and a spread. Each monthly value is treated as the month's mid-point, with straight lines between them.
Search results are the news before 1 Feb 2024 on robusta and Vietnam's harvest.

The model has seen this period. Nemotron Ultra's model card gives a pre-training cutoff of September 2025 and a post-training cutoff of May 2026, so a date in the prompt cannot make it forget. The run only gives it news from before the date, and the leak check looks for hindsight in what it wrote.

“Best plan in hindsight” is the best of about 230 plans on a fixed grid (price, start, end, extra stock), run on the real path. Shoppers react to a sweep plan like they did to the nearest price plan the analysis tested; with none tested, they are neutral.
News pages are read as they are today. Any article that names a date after the as-of date is dropped, but a page edited later could still carry hindsight.
